pages.api:
# API reference

> The readings, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Reading `transcript/<name>`

`transcript.v1`, class `reading`: `source_id`, `node_id`, `t_ns` (utterance start), `seq`, `text` (at most 4096 chars), `lang`, `start_ns`, `end_ns` (capture clock of the stream), `confidence` (always 1.0: not measured).

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `utterances`, `transcripts`, `errors`, `audio` (s), `asr.time` (s), `chunks.skipped`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout

A line `{"heard": "...", "audio_ms": N, "asr_ms": N}` per transcript, then one report per interval:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `recognizer` | string | the model, `synthetic`, `none` |
| `utterances`, `transcripts`, `empty`, `errors` | numbers | since start |
| `audio_s`, `asr_ms_mean`, `real_time_factor` | numbers | decode time over audio time |
| `noise_floor_dbfs`, `speaking` | number, bool | the segmenter's state |
| `last_text`, `last_error` | string/null | |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `streaming`, `published`, `skipped_chunks`, `error` |

## Store vector (id 33)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `transcripts` | count |
| 1 | `rtf` | decode time / audio time |
| 2 | `asr_ms_mean` | ms |
| 3 | `noise_floor_dbfs` | dBFS |
| 4 | `audio_s` | seconds heard |
| 5 | `skipped_chunks` | count |
| 6 | `bus_connected` | 0 or 1 |
| 7 | `errors` | count |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8067`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw` (latest raw view), `/history` (last 60 reports), `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--source`, `--name`, `--lang`, `--margin-db`, `--min-db`, `--hang-ms`, `--min-ms`, `--max-ms`, `--threads`, `--python`, `--model-dir`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.model:
# The model

> What runs the recognition, and where it lives.

The cog starts one worker process and talks to it in JSON lines. The worker is a short Python script carried inside the cog (`worker/asr_worker.py`); it loads the **Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2** model, int8-quantised, through **sherpa-onnx** and decodes each utterance on the CPU.

| Needs | Default |
|---|---|
| Python with `sherpa_onnx` and `numpy` | `$ASR_PYTHON`, else `/data/bench/venv/bin/python` |
| Model directory with `encoder.int8.onnx`, `decoder.int8.onnx`, `joiner.int8.onnx`, `tokens.txt` | `/data/bench/models/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8` |

Set **Python** and **Model directory** in the settings for another location. Start-up takes a few seconds while the model loads; the report says `no_source` until it has.

The worker writes nothing; the cog saves each utterance to a small file in its data directory (four files, reused) and sends the path.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-asr --once --replay phrase.wav            # the file through the real recognizer
cog-asr --once --window 10                    # listen to the broker's mic stream for 10 s
cog-asr                                       # continuous; status on :8067
```

With `WEFTOS_COGBUS` and `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN` set (the host sets them for a placed cog) the cog subscribes to the microphone stream and publishes transcripts. Each heard utterance is also printed as a JSON line `{"heard": ...}`.

## Placed on a node

Place `asr` in the same project as `audio-in`. Its `cog.toml` declares the input `audio.pcm` and the outputs `transcript` and `telemetry`. It declares no device, so any number of listeners may read the same stream.

## Needs

- The model and Python described in **The model**.
- About 1 GB of memory while the model is loaded.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Turn the microphone stream into text that other cogs can read.

`asr` listens to `audio.pcm/<source>` (the `audio-in` cog's stream), cuts it into utterances, transcribes each and publishes a `transcript.v1` reading on `transcript/<name>` (default `asr0`). A wake-word or assistant cog subscribes to those transcripts.

## The short path

1. **Have a microphone stream.** Run `audio-in`. → see its guide
2. **Check the model.** The Parakeet files and a Python with sherpa-onnx must exist. → see **The model**
3. **Try it on a file.** `cog-asr --once --replay phrase.wav` prints the transcript. → see **Set up**
4. **Place it.** It reads the stream and publishes. → see **Set up**

You can test with no model: `--once --simulate` runs two synthetic tone bursts through the whole path and reports their length, marked `SYNTHETIC`.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- Speech is found by energy, then confirmed by the transcript. The first second after start is spent learning the room, and nothing is heard in it.
- Utterances are transcribed one at a time on the CPU. With three threads Parakeet runs about 8 times faster than real time, so a 4 s phrase takes about half a second; a long utterance delays the next.
- Parakeet reports no confidence. Every transcript says `confidence: 1.0`, which means not measured.
- The model is English only.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

The report's `error` says why.

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `the recognizer worker did not become ready` | the model or Python is missing, or loading took over two minutes | check **The model**; run the worker by hand: `python asr_worker.py MODEL_DIR 3` |
| `<path>: No such file or directory` | the Python path is wrong | set **Python** |

## No transcripts although people are talking

- `noise_floor_dbfs` very high (above -35): a loud room or a hot microphone raises the bar. Lower the capture gain.
- `speaking` never true: raise sensitivity with a lower **Speech margin**, or lower **Speech floor**.
- `empty` grows: the recognizer heard noise, not speech. That is the second stage working.

## Transcripts are cut in the middle of a sentence

A pause longer than **Hangover** (600 ms) ends the utterance. Raise it.

## `skipped_chunks` grows

The recognizer was busy longer than the stream's ring holds (about 130 s) or the reader fell behind. Reduce the recognizer's load.

## `errors` grows

`last_error` holds the worker's message. The worker keeps serving after an error.

toml:
# Sensor guide for asr (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "Speech recognition on a Linux board"
sensor = "Microphone stream from audio-in, recognized on the CPU"
cog = "asr"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "model", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
model = "model"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "audio.pcm stream"
detail = "16 kHz mono, 20 ms chunks"

[[flow]]
name = "Segmenter"
detail = "noise floor, hangover"

[[flow]]
name = "Parakeet worker"
detail = "sherpa-onnx int8, CPU"

[[flow]]
name = "Outputs"
detail = "transcript.v1, telemetry, :8067"
